Logistics

Getting there, getting home

Point-to-point: Ride out of Grand Central, bike back to the city. No car required.

Start: Peekskill via Metro-North

The 7:55 am Hudson Line toward Beacon, from Grand Central or Harlem-125th St. Roll straight off the platform onto Route 202 along the river.

Aim to be at Grand Central by 7:30.

Finish: Strictly Bicycles, Fort Lee

A few of us will ride back from here to BK, but Strictly is official ride end.

The ride

Six chapters, north to south

We're climbing hard early while it's cool, then chill spin home along the water.

1
Mi 0 – 5.4

Peekskill to the Bear Mountain Bridge

Off the train and straight onto the Goat Path: Routes 202/6 carved into the bluff above the Hudson. It rolls upward with big river views almost immediately. The shoulder is narrow from mile 1.4, so ride single file and hold a steady line. Cross the Bear Mountain Bridge (take the walkway if traffic is heavy), then navigate the traffic circle on the far side with care.

Mi 1.4–5.4 · narrow shoulder Mi 5.4 · Bear Mtn circle
2
Mi 5.4 – 12.7

Perkins Memorial Drive

Quick bathroom stop at the Bear Mountain Inn, then climb Bear Mtn. Perkins Memorial Drive to the tower at roughly 1,305 feet, the high point of the day at mile 10.5. It comes early and it is long, so we'll take it cheeeeel and enjoy the view. The descent has hairpins: drops, brakes, space between riders.

Mi 6 · Bear Mtn Inn (water + bathrooms) Mi 10.5–12.7 · hairpin descent
3
Mi 12.7 – 20

Down the river road

Off the Perkins descent and back past Bear Mountain to the Hudson, then south along the water on 9W past Iona Island, ducking off onto Old Jones Point Road and Old Ayers Road, the quiet old alignments that keep us off the highway for most of it, into Tomkins Cove and West Shore Drive. NYCC vetoed the old Route 6 entrance into the park, so we take the scenic way around.

Mi 15.2–19.7 · short 9W stretches, single file
4
Mi 20 – 33

The Harriman lakes

Into the park the back way: a sharp right onto Mott Farm Road with a punchy kicker, then Queensboro Road past the old Letchworth grounds, Cedar Flats, and the long Gate Hill and Kanawauke climb to the day's second summit around 750 feet. We roll the south shore of Lake Welch, with water and restrooms at the beach around mile 29, then drop out of the park on Willow Grove Road toward Thiells.

Mi 19.8 · Mott Farm sharp right + kicker Mi 29 · Lake Welch (water)
5
Mi 33 – 50

Hook Mountain gravel and the river villages

Through Thiells and Garnerville into Haverstraw, where mile 36.8 offers an optional refuel before the gravel: a quick deli sandwich, or Big Daddy's Home Plate BBQ right where the route crosses 9W. Then the route leaves the road for the Hook Mountain and Nyack Beach river trail: roughly three miles of gravel pinned between the Palisades cliffs and the water. The Haverstraw half is the rough half, rocky and steep in places with real cliff exposure, and walking the worst pitch is completely fine. It spits you out into Nyack for the lunch stop: the Runcible Spoon on North Broadway at mile 47.1, the classic cyclist bakery. Then an easy spin down to Piermont and its pier.

Mi 36.8 · Haverstraw deli or Big Daddy's BBQ Mi 40–44.5 · loose gravel, cliff exposure Mi 47.1 · Runcible Spoon (lunch)
6
Mi 50 – 66.1

Sparkill, the 9W Market, and the ridge home

From Piermont through Sparkill onto the Rockland Road climb, about 450 feet back up to the Palisades ridge and the 9W Market in Palisades, NY: the classic last stop for food and bathrooms at mile 53.1. Then 9W south along the ridge, rolling between 400 and 500 feet with traffic that deserves respect, onto Hudson Terrace, past the George Washington Bridge, and into Strictly Bicycles for the finish-line espresso.

Mi 53.1 · 9W Market Mi 54–63 · 9W traffic GWB path entry Mi 66.1 · Strictly Bicycles

Study hall

Every. Single. Turn.

A wise SIG leader once decreed that a prepared rider studies every turn of the route on Google Street View before the ride. Who are we to argue. All 60 turns, in order, camera pointed the way we'll be riding.

Refuel

The stops

Six planned, roughly one every 90 minutes. Lake Welch is the last water in the park, lunch is Nyack or Haverstraw, and the 9W Market is the last food before the finish. We can skip any we feel like.

MI 6.0

Bear Mountain Inn

Water fountains and bathrooms at Hessian Lake. Last fill-up before Perkins.

MI 29

Lake Welch

Water and restrooms at the beach. Fill both bottles.

MI 36.8

Haverstraw: deli or BBQ

Optional. Deli sandwiches for speed, or Big Daddy's Home Plate BBQ for a proper lunch.

MI 47.1

Runcible Spoon

Nyack. The classic cyclist bakery: sandwiches, coffee, bathrooms, racks out front.

MI 53.1

9W Market

Palisades, NY. Food and bathrooms, the classic stop.

MI 66.1

Strictly Bicycles

Fort Lee. Espresso. Done.

Plan B

Escape hatches

Turn back at the bridge

Mile ~5. If the legs or the weather say no, roll back down the Goat Path to Peekskill station. Trains run all day.

Skip Perkins

Mile ~8. Perkins Memorial Drive is a dead-end spur off Seven Lakes Drive that ends at the tower, so the bail-out is simply not turning: stay on Seven Lakes Drive and the group catches you on the far side. Saves about 5 miles and 900 feet of climbing.

Skip the gravel

Mile ~40. Stay on Broadway/9W from Haverstraw to Nyack instead of the river trail. Similar distance, all pavement, more traffic.

Bail to Tarrytown

Mile ~46 (South Nyack). The Cuomo Bridge shared-use path entrance is at 1200 Route 9W in South Nyack, inside Thruway Interchange 10, open 6 am to 10 pm. It's 3.6 miles across to the Tarrytown side (333 South Broadway), then about a mile to Tarrytown station and the Hudson Line home.

Ride notes

How we're riding it

Pacing Perkins

This is a medium-low spice ride. Bear comes at mile 8 with 60 miles still to go and we're going to take it chill. Settle in, spin, talk.

Gravel handling

28mm or wider tires are ideal for the Hook Mountain trail. Stay loose on the bars, and let the bike move under you. The Haverstraw half is rocky and steep; walking the worst pitch is fine and nobody will remember.

Descending

The two descents that matter are Perkins (hairpins) and Willow Grove Road out of the park (fast and residential). Ride both cautiously: hands in the drops, brake before the turn, leave space, and call out holes for the rider behind you.

Curriculum

Skills we'll be practicing

  1. Don't crash
  2. Don't blow up the ride
  3. Have fun
  4. Good vibes
